jp: 駅[えき]で友達[ともだち]を{待[ま]って|nt-n5}います。
en: I am waiting for a friend at the station.
why: Waiting is 待つ; the left part is ぎょうにんべん (the going radical), not a hand or a cow.

jp: かばんを二[ふた]つ{持[も]って|nt-n5}います。
en: I am carrying two bags.
why: Holding or carrying is 持つ; the left part is the hand radical.

jp: この{特別[とくべつ]|nt-n5}な日[ひ]に、みんなで写真[しゃしん]を撮[と]りました。
en: On this special day we all took a photo together.
why: Special is 特別; the left part is the ushihen (cow radical).

jp: 公園[こうえん]に{大[おお]きい|nt-n5}木[き]があります。
en: There is a big tree in the park.
why: Big is 大きい, a plain 大 with no extra stroke or dot.

jp: この{太[ふと]い|nt-n5}ペンで名前[なまえ]を書[か]いてください。
en: Please write your name with this thick pen.
why: Thick is 太い: 大 with an extra dot underneath.

jp: {犬[いぬ]|nt-n5}と散歩[さんぽ]に行[い]きます。
en: I go for a walk with my dog.
why: Dog is 犬: 大 with a dot at the upper right.

jp: {右[みぎ]|nt-n5}に曲[ま]がると、銀行[ぎんこう]があります。
en: If you turn right, there is a bank.
why: Right is 右: the slanting stroke is written first and pokes up above the top bar, while in 石 it starts at the bar.

jp: 川[かわ]で小[ちい]さい{石[いし]|nt-n5}を拾[ひろ]いました。
en: I picked up a small stone at the river.
why: Stone is 石: the top bar comes first and the slanting stroke starts from it without poking above, unlike 右.

jp: {木[き]|nt-n5}の下[した]で本[ほん]を読[よ]みます。
en: I read a book under the tree.
why: Tree is 木 with no extra stroke across it.

jp: 図書館[としょかん]で{本[ほん]|nt-n5}を三冊[さんさつ]借[か]りました。
en: I borrowed three books at the library.
why: Book is 本: 木 with one stroke added at the base of the trunk.

jp: 広場[ひろば]に{人[ひと]|nt-n5}がたくさん並[なら]んでいます。
en: Lots of people are lined up in the square.
why: Person is 人, where the left stroke is the longer one that reaches the top.

jp: 部屋[へや]に{入[はい]る|nt-n5}前[まえ]に、くつをぬいでください。
en: Please take off your shoes before you enter the room.
why: Enter is 入る, where the right stroke is the longer one.

jp: この切符[きっぷ]は{千[せん]|nt-n5}円[えん]です。
en: This ticket costs one thousand yen.
why: Thousand is 千, a slanted stroke on top of 十.

jp: 洗[あら]ったシャツを外[そと]に{干[ほ]します|nt-n5}。
en: I hang the washed shirts outside to dry.
why: Drying laundry is 干す, written with 干 (the horizontal stroke on top is straight).

jp: 庭[にわ]の{土[つち]|nt-n5}はやわらかいです。
en: The soil in the garden is soft.
why: Soil is 土, where the lower horizontal stroke is the longer one.

jp: 来週[らいしゅう]の{土曜日[どようび]|nt-n5}は休[やす]みです。
en: Next Saturday is a day off.
why: Saturday is 土曜日; 土 has the longer stroke at the bottom.

jp: 夏[なつ]に{富士山[ふじさん]|nt-n5}に登[のぼ]りました。
en: I climbed Mount Fuji in the summer.
why: Fuji is written 富士山; 士 has the longer stroke at the top, the reverse of 土.

jp: 電話[でんわ]が終[お]わるまで、少[すこ]し{待[ま]って|nt-n5}ください。
en: Please wait a little until the phone call is over.
why: Asking someone to wait is 待ってください, with 待 (the going radical).

jp: 重[おも]い荷物[にもつ]を{持[も]って|nt-n5}あげます。
en: I will carry the heavy luggage for you.
why: Carrying a load is 持つ; the hand radical is on the left.

jp: {大[おお]きな|nt-n5}声[こえ]で話[はな]さないでください。
en: Please do not speak in a loud voice.
why: Big (as in loud) is 大きな; no dot is needed.

jp: {大学[だいがく]|nt-n5}で日本語[にほんご]を勉強[べんきょう]しています。
en: I am studying Japanese at university.
why: University is 大学; 大 is the plain big character.

jp: うちの{子犬[こいぬ]|nt-n5}が生[う]まれました。
en: Our puppies have been born.
why: Puppy is 子犬; the dot of 犬 marks the animal.

jp: 最近[さいきん]、少[すこ]し{太[ふと]りました|nt-n5}。
en: I have put on a little weight lately.
why: Getting fat is 太る, written with 太 (dot under 大).

jp: 字[じ]は{右手[みぎて]|nt-n5}で書[か]きます。
en: I write characters with my right hand.
why: Right hand is 右手, with 右 for right; 左 would mean left hand.

jp: 母[はは]は{宝石[ほうせき]|nt-n5}が好[す]きです。
en: My mother likes jewels.
why: Jewel is 宝石, with 石 for stone.

jp: 駅[えき]の前[まえ]に{本屋[ほんや]|nt-n5}があります。
en: There is a bookshop in front of the station.
why: Bookshop is 本屋; 本 has the extra stroke at the base of 木.

jp: {日本[にほん]|nt-n5}の夏[なつ]は暑[あつ]いです。
en: Summer in Japan is hot.
why: Japan is 日本, ending in 本 (book, origin).

jp: {木曜日[もくようび]|nt-n5}に歯医者[はいしゃ]へ行[い]きます。
en: I go to the dentist on Thursday.
why: Thursday is 木曜日, written with the plain tree character 木.

jp: {入口[いりぐち]|nt-n5}はあちらです。
en: The entrance is over there.
why: Entrance is 入口, with 入 whose right stroke is longer.

jp: 東京[とうきょう]の{人口[じんこう]|nt-n5}はとても多[おお]いです。
en: The population of Tokyo is very large.
why: Population is 人口, with 人 for person, not 入.

jp: あの{外国人[がいこくじん]|nt-n5}は日本語[にほんご]が上手[じょうず]です。
en: That foreigner is good at Japanese.
why: Foreigner is 外国人, ending in 人 (person).

jp: この本[ほん]は{二千[にせん]|nt-n5}円[えん]でした。
en: This book cost two thousand yen.
why: Two thousand is 二千; 千 has a slanted stroke over 十.

jp: 雨[あめ]が降[ふ]る前[まえ]に、シャツを{干[ほ]して|nt-n5}ください。
en: Please hang the shirts out to dry before it rains.
why: Hanging out to dry is 干す; the top stroke of 干 is horizontal.

jp: 旅行[りょこう]の{お土産[おみやげ]|nt-n5}を買[か]いました。
en: I bought souvenirs on the trip.
why: Souvenir is お土産, with 土 (earth) as its first kanji.

jp: いい{気持[きも]ち|nt-n5}で目[め]が覚[さ]めました。
en: I woke up feeling good.
why: Feeling is 気持ち, with 持 (hand radical) as in holding a feeling.

jp: {待[ま]ち合[あ]わせ|nt-n5}の時間[じかん]は三時[さんじ]です。
en: The meeting time is three o'clock.
why: A meeting arrangement is 待ち合わせ, built on 待つ (to wait).

jp: {特急[とっきゅう]|nt-n5}に乗[の]ると、早[はや]く着[つ]きます。
en: If you take the limited express, you arrive sooner.
why: Limited express is 特急, with 特 (cow radical) meaning special.

jp: 家族[かぞく]は{大切[たいせつ]|nt-n5}です。
en: My family is important to me.
why: Important is 大切, written with the plain 大.

jp: {大人[おとな]|nt-n5}は五百円[ごひゃくえん]です。
en: The adult fee is five hundred yen.
why: Adult is 大人 (big person); 犬 would be a dog.

jp: {三人[さんにん]|nt-n5}で映画[えいが]を見[み]に行[い]きました。
en: The three of us went to see a film.
why: Three people is 三人, with 人 for person.

jp: 先生[せんせい]が教室[きょうしつ]に{入[はい]って|nt-n5}きました。
en: The teacher came into the classroom.
why: Entering is 入る, with 入 (right stroke longer).

jp: {右[みぎ]|nt-n5}の足[あし]が少[すこ]し痛[いた]いです。
en: My right foot hurts a little.
why: Right (side) is 右; 左 would be left and 石 is a stone.

jp: {本当[ほんとう]|nt-n5}ですか。
en: Is that really true?
why: Truly is 本当, with 本 (木 plus a base stroke).
